programme.title: Voyages of Discovery

programme.title: Kabul

programme.title: To the Manor Born

programme.title: Deep, Down and Dirty: The Science of Soil
programme.desc: Gardening expert Chris Beardshaw explores where soil comes from, and what it is made of. It is an often misunderstood substance, with people sometimes dismissing it as dirt, so he reveals it as it has never been seen before using specialist microphotography, and highlights what makes it so essential to life. Research shows that humans are pushing this precious resource to its limit, and scientists are battling to find ways of preserving it for the future

programme.desc: Situated north of the Arctic Circle, the Lofoten Islands in Norway are famed for their dramatic mountain landscapes and cod fisheries. Coinneach arrives MacLeod in March during peak cod season, helping to unload the day's catch and observing the stockfish drying process. He works with a local chef to create a fine-dining dish using the wind-dried cod, makes lefse, a traditional flatbread, and harvests seaweed. A dinner of Lofotlam, a globally protected local lamb, rounds off his visit

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara (Mermaid Tales)
programme.desc: Kate MacLeod, aka The Hebridean Mermaid, explores the hidden gems of the Hebrides, meeting tradition bearers with remarkable stories about the places she loves to visit the most, above and below the water. In this episode she comes across an interesting sea creature, known as a sunfish, which is native to tropical waters, but is likely to have been carried to the islands by the Gulf Stream. Swimming on its side, the sun heats its body and it feeds on jellyfish. She also journeys to Taransay, home of some of the most stunning and unique beaches in the Outer Hebrides. Once a thriving community, the island had three villages, but is now home to deer, seabirds and cattle.

programme.title: Faodail: Found
programme.desc: The Faodail Film Archive, which gathers lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s to the 1980s in the Outer Hebrides, storing the footage for future generations. The Cinema Sgre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online, and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gidhealtachd for contemporary audiences

Forty years on from the disaster, Jordan Dunbar travels to Chernobyl to examine the events that led to the world's worst nuclear accident and what we can learn from them today.

programme.title: World's Ultimate Adventures
programme.desc: Chef and content creator Julie Lin is on a Turkish adventure - combining her passion for food with history. Travelling through the south east, known as the gastronomic heart, she first stops in the city of Gazianetep - world famous for its baklava. Julie uncovers what makes this delicacy and the locally grown pistachios inside it so special. Heading further east, she visits the Neolithic site of Karahan Tepe, a discovery so significant that it is reshaping our understanding of human history. Guided by the archaeological team, Julie explores their latest finds, including what may be the world's oldest kitchen. Her journey ends in ?anl?urfa, cooking with a family keeping traditional recipes alive, discovering the city's signature smoked pepper, and finishing her trip with a vibrant cultural, night-time celebration and an unusual raw-meat dish.

programme.desc: In a forest in East Ayrshire, paramedics struggle to treat a man who has suffered a traumatic injury in a mountain bike accident, with specialist equipment having to be brought in

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson and Brian Cunningham tackle viewers' questions and also start a major new project as they launch a makeover of an area at Beechgrove called the Crooked Garden. One of the first parts of that revamp is the creation of a stumpery, a growing technique based on an old tree and planted with a range of ferns. George has details on feeding cherry trees right now, Brian is back in the 8x6 greenhouse, and there is a visit to St Andrews Botanic Garden

programme.title: Reporting Scotland: News at Seven

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: The Barclays are finding their feet with their new business, which involves buying lambs to fatten up for the butcher. Rachel and Camy, who are one year into their tenancy, set off to market at Lairg to buy more ewes, while Nikki and Ollie find out if their favourite buffalo is pregnant

programme.title: Murder Trial: Death of a Dog Walker
programme.desc: Part two of two. With Brian Low's family desperately seeking justice and answers, the fate of ex-gamekeeper David Campbell hangs in the balance. Witnesses unearth more shocking revelations and the defendant takes the stand before the jury must answer the ultimate question of his guilt. The court is shown dramatic footage from Campbell's custody interview where tempers flared when allegations were put to him, with the prosecution pointing to a guilty man on the ropes, while the defence argue it shows a police force under pressure to get their man

programme.title: David Wilson's Crime Files
programme.desc: The criminologist and guests delve into the psychology of criminals who lead a secret or double life, hiding behind a respectable or constructed front in order to cover up their illegal activities. In a short film, investigative journalist Fiona Walker takes viewers back to 18th-century Edinburgh to tell the infamous tale of Willie Brodie, town councillor by day, criminal mastermind by night

programme.title: Scotcast

With contributions from McAllister himself, as well as Steven Gerrard, Gordon Strachan and Ardal O'Hanlon

programme.title: Live EFL
programme.desc: Notts County v Leicester City (Kick-off 12.00pm). Coverage of the League One match at Meadow Lane. It has been a turbulent few years for Leicester, who have endured financial difficulties and been relegated in each of the last two seasons. In contrast, the Magpies were playing non-league football three seasons ago, but have been promoted twice since then to reach the third tier for the first time since the 2014/15 campaign

programme.title: Live EFL
programme.desc: York City v Bristol Rovers (Kick-off 3.00pm). Coverage of both teams' opening League Two match of the season, held at LNER Community Stadium. York won the National League last term to secure a place in the Football League since they were relegated in the 2015/16 season, but their title-winning manager Stuart Maynard departed during the summer and was replaced by Scott Lindsey. Their opponents will be looking to improve on last season's 14th-place finish and push for promotion

programme.title: Live EFL
programme.desc: Sheffield United v Birmingham City (kick-off 5.30pm). Coverage of both teams' opening match of the Championship season, held at Bramall Lane. United claimed a 3-0 win in last season's corresponding fixture thanks to goals by Tyler Bindon, Gustavo Hamer and Patrick Bamford, but Birmingham were reduced to 10 men in the 18th minute due to Tommy Doyle's red card when the score was 1-0

Coverage of day six of the joint ATP 1000 and WTA 1000 event, a hard-court tournament at Lindner Family Tennis Center in Mason, Ohio, where the third round is scheduled to conclude. Alexei Popyrin and Andrey Rublev were involved in the match of the round in last year's men's draw, which saw the latter come out on top via a 6-7 7-6 7-5 score. The number two seed Carlos Alcaraz had an easier time of things as he triumphed 6-4 6-4 against Hamad Medjedovic to book his place in the last-16

programme.title: Live Tennis
programme.desc: The Cincinnati Open. Further coverage of day six of the joint ATP 1000 and WTA 1000 event, a hard-court tournament at Lindner Family Tennis Center in Mason, Ohio. Magda Linette claimed a surprise 7-6 3-6 6-3 win over the number four seed Jessica Pegula at the corresponding stage 12 months ago, while the second seed Coco Gauff benefited from a walkover victory when Dayana Yastremska had to withdraw from their match without taking to the court
